language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

My first assignment involves the different states of matter. Did you know that matter can exist as  solid, liquid or gas and that matter can change from one state to another depending on temperature and pressure?
For example: a solid can melt into a liquid. I need to match the different types of matter with their states.
Can you help me?

In science class I learned that matter can undergo changes that can be permanent or temporary. A permanent change is irreversible and forms new products. A temporary change is reversible and no new products are formed. In this assignment my teacher wants me to determine whether each statement is true or false.

helperSimple.text: Andrew's teacher has asked him to determine whether the statements are true or false. Can you help him?

activities.subtitle: When I accidentally drop my plate and it breaks, I changed the plate permanently.

activities.subtitle: When my mom bakes cookies from using several ingredients that change is temporary.

activities.subtitle: When an egg is fried that change is permanent.

activities.subtitle: When ice melts that change is permament.

outro.text: Fantastic! Thank you for your help.
